html:
The siege of Chandax in 960 and 961 won the island of Crete back for the Byzantine Empire after about 135 years of Muslim rule. Chandax was the capital of the Emirate of Crete, on the site of modern Heraklion.

Arab exiles from al-Andalus had taken Crete in the 820s, and from there their fleets raided the Aegean for more than a century. Several Byzantine attempts to win it back had failed, the last in 949. In 960 Romanos II sent a great fleet under the general Nikephoros Phokas, armed with Greek fire.

The army landed, beat the Arabs in the field and settled down to a siege through a hard winter. In March 961 the walls were stormed and the city was sacked. Nikephoros came home to a triumph in Constantinople, and two years later he was emperor. Crete was resettled and Christian missionaries were sent, and the Aegean became safer for Byzantine ships.
sum: The siege of Chandax in 960 and 961 won the island of Crete back for the Byzantine Empire after about 135 years of Muslim rule. Chandax was the capital of the Emirate of Crete, on the site of modern Heraklion.
